item.title: 🔴 Exploit Attempts for GPUStack Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-102895), (Thu, Nov 12th)
item.description:
Why this matters: Authentication bypass — review access controls and look for unauthorized access.

CVE-2026-102895 is a trivial authentication-bypass vulnerability. GPUStack is also an attractive target. It is open-source software that manages clusters of GPUs, which are typically used to run AI workloads. All versions of GPUStack prior to 2.2.0, which was released at the end of June. This vulnerability was not made public until the end of July, and the CVE was assigned on November 4th.



Source: SANS Internet Storm Center  |  Severity: Critical  |  Age: 5h

item.title: 🔴 Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
item.description:
Why this matters: Elevated ransomware risk — validate backups, endpoint protection, and recovery readiness.
The cybercrime group Qilin has emerged as the world's most active ransomware affiliate program, claiming at least 365 victim organizations in the past three months alone. But even top Russian hackers make operational security mistakes, and the administrator of Qilin has made a few key missteps over the last decade that all point to a 36-year-old man living in St. Petersburg, Russia.

item.title: 🟠 Microsoft Patches 1,259 Flaws, Including Exploited Outlook Bug That May Expose NTLMv2 Hashes
item.description:
Why this matters: Could affect email access or mail flow — monitor delivery and Outlook behavior.
Microsoft on Tuesday released patches for a total of 1,259 vulnerabilities spanning its software portfolio, the second consecutive month where the patch volume has exceeded 1,000 flaws. These cover 726 flaws in Windows, 174 in Office, 61 in Developer Tools, 59 in SQL Server, 53 in Developer Tools, and 27 in SharePoint Server. The patches also include 165 non-Microsoft-issued CVE identifiers.

Source: The Hacker News  |  Severity: Important  |  Age: 1d

item.title: 🟠 Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities
item.description:
Why this matters: Could affect email access or mail flow — monitor delivery and Outlook behavior.
Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month's Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws -- including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook -- and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe, Apple, Google and Mozilla.

Source: Krebs on Security  |  Severity: Important  |  Age: 1d
